body.heading: About this sheet
paragraphs: Free SparkKindly Kids matching & sorting printable: Match the Pictures 08.
Pictures to match to their partners — draw a line from each picture to the one that belongs with it.

body.heading: How to use it
paragraphs: Print the sheet, name each picture out loud first, then draw the matching lines. Talking about WHY two things match is where the thinking happens.

takeaway: Matching and sorting are the roots of maths, reading and science — spotting what is the same and what is different.
materials: Safety scissors if you would rather cut the pictures out and move them
supervision: Ask for the reason, not just the line — "they match because…" turns a worksheet into a conversation.
safetyNotes: Use child-safe scissors with rounded tips, and sit at a table while cutting. Keep small cut pieces away from children under 3 — they are a choking hazard.
Print at 100% size (not "fit to page") so the sheet keeps its true size and the pictures stay the size they were drawn.
screenFreeExtension: Sort a real drawer together — socks, spoons or crayons — into matching groups, then mess it up and race to sort it again.
